items.title: Norway and Finland leaders hold rare call with Putin
items.description: An end to the conflict in Ukraine "will not be achieved through silence," Finland's President Alexander Stubb said.

items.title: Ceasefire extended across Ukraine's Kherson region, officials say
items.description: The truce was originally planned for the stranded residents of Oleshky, and Russia and Ukraine say no breaches have been reported.

items.title: Mbappé sorry for 'ill-judged' Mao remark after backlash in China
items.description: The France star had referred to the former Chinese leader as a "dictator" during an interview about memes.

items.title: Lula's comeback in Brazil dents Trump's ambitions for Latin America
items.description: The Trump-Lula relationship may have thawed, but several issues could reignite tensions between the two leaders.

items.title: Dutch zookeeper dies after being mauled by leopard
items.description: The woman began her career at the park when she was 17 and had worked there on-and-off for four decades.

items.title: Ex-wife of Zimbabwe's vice-president freed after collapse of attempted murder case
items.description: Marry Mubaiwa had been held on remand for seven years after being charged in 2019 for her then husband's attempted murder.

items.title: Alexander brothers each sentenced to 30 years in prison for sex trafficking case
items.description: The three brothers were found guilty of drugging and raping several women over the course of decades.

items.title: Egypt court fines journalist Lina Attalah and orders news site's closure
items.description: Amnesty International said the verdict against Attalah and independent outlet Mada Masr represented "a crushing blow to press freedom".

items.title: Ghanaian twin brothers and US woman plead guilty to $9m romance scam
items.description: The group targeted elderly people across US and Europe, luring them into romantic relationship before persuading them to transfer large sums of money.

items.title: Ballon d'Or ceremony raises case of French sports journalist jailed in Algeria
items.description: He is in jail accused of supporting terrorism after travelling to the politically sensitive region Kabylie.

items.title: Deaths in detention cells in Nigeria were entirely preventable, inquiry finds
items.description: Overcrowding and poor ventilation caused the deaths of 33 detainees in a prison cell in Minna state.

items.title: Controversial Islamic cleric shot dead in northern Nigeria
items.description: Yahaya Masussuka had posted videos in which he rejected some elements of mainstream Islam.

items.title: Jordan carries out deadly strike in Syria in retaliation for church attack
items.description: The attack on a village in Syria killed five people, including women and children, Syrian health officials said.

items.title: West warns of famine risk in Sudan as civil war grinds on
items.description: Millions face acute hunger in Sudan as conflict, drought and funding cuts aggravate the humanitarian crisis.

items.title: Nanotyrannus skeleton sells for $47.3m in New York auction
items.description: The sale of the rare skeleton reignites debate in the scientific community about whether dinosaur remains should end up in private hands or public view.

items.title: Ex-FBI chief James Comey faces federal charges for third time
items.description: Comey's lawyers say the case stems from alleged disclosure of classified information to the New York Times in 2016.

items.title: Jay-Z to perform at Super Bowl half-time show
items.description: The rapper has been involved with the show for years but has never before performed at the NFL championship game.

items.title: Netherlands pulls out of Eurovision again over Israel participation
items.description: A Dutch broadcaster reverses a decision to take part, citing "sensitivities" over Israel's participation.

items.title: Watch: The Mbappé-Chairman Mao controversy explained
items.description: Kylian Mbappé has apologised for "ill-judged" comments he made about late Chinese leader Mao Zedong.

items.title: What does Israel's election mean for Gaza and the wider world?
items.description: The BBC's diplomatic correspondent James Landale reports from Jerusalem as ballots are cast.
